Module 1: Getting Started with Google Workspace

Learn what Google Workspace is, sign in safely, move between Drive, Docs, Sheets, and Slides, and work with the Microsoft Office files people send you.

4
Lessons
80
Minutes
4
Practice simulations
Beginner
Level

What You'll Learn

  • What each Google Workspace app is for, and which Microsoft 365 app does the same job
  • How a personal Google account differs from a work or school account
  • How to sign in with 2-Step Verification and sign out safely on a shared computer
  • How to use the Google apps menu, app home screens, templates, and Search the menus
  • How to edit, convert, and download Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files in Google Workspace

Real-World Scenario

You just started as the office assistant at Parkview Property Management, a small company that manages Elm Street Apartments and Riverside Commons. Everyone at Parkview works in Google Workspace. Your manager, Denise Carter, set up your account and wants you ready on day one: signing in on the shared front desk computer, finding the team's files, starting new ones, and handling the Word and Excel files that vendors and tenants still send.

Lessons

Complete each lesson in order. Watch the slideshow, read the notes, try the practice simulation, and finish the challenge.

Lesson 1⏱ 20 min
🧭

What Google Workspace Is

Meet the Google Workspace apps, learn how a personal Google account differs from a work account, and see how each Google app lines up with the Microsoft 365 app you may already know.

Lesson 2⏱ 20 min
🧭

Signing In and Keeping Your Account Safe

Sign in to your Google account, approve a 2-Step Verification prompt, and sign out the right way on a shared or public computer.

Lesson 3⏱ 20 min
🧭

Getting Around Drive, Docs, Sheets, and Slides

Move between the Google apps, start a new file from a blank page or a template, and learn the parts of the screen that every Google editor shares.

Lesson 4⏱ 20 min
🧭

Working with Microsoft Office Files

Open and edit Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files without converting them, convert one to a Google file when you need to, and download Google files as Office files or PDFs.
